abstraction_design.rationale: The real variation is mostly captured (PokemonCard, MoveTables, EvolutionTree are well-shaped), but list pages and detail-page data functions are parallel copies rather than a stretchable abstraction, so similar-but-different cases mean duplication.

findings.issue: Every page-data function returns `any`, and every page consumes the payload untyped, so the internal server↔page contract is implicit; a renamed field fails only at render time.
findings.suggestion: Define payload interfaces in Nuxt 4's `shared/` directory (auto-imported by both app and server) and type the return values; Nuxt 4.6's typed $fetch/useFetch will then propagate them to the pages.

findings.issue: `findSpeciesSummary` is dead code while the identical `index.species.find(...)` lookup is inlined at lines 451, 487 and 526.
findings.suggestion: Delete the helper or (better) use it in the three page functions so a lookup change (e.g. alternate-form handling) lands once.

findings.issue: The type-label Map is built identically five times (lines 161, 230, 282, 442, 516).
findings.suggestion: Extract a `getTypeLabels()` helper returning the Map and reuse it everywhere.

findings.issue: The Pokémon-card list wrapper (count line + ul.card-grid + v-for) is duplicated on four pages, so a cross-cutting change like sorting touches every list separately.
findings.suggestion: Extract a `PokemonCardList` component that owns the count, list and (future) sort controls; pages pass the array of species summaries.

findings.issue: Not-found handling is repeated on every detail page (`v-if="!data?.found"` plus a title fallback computed) alongside NotFoundPage.vue's own useHead, giving two sources of truth for the 'Not found – Pokédex' title.
findings.suggestion: Have server handlers `throw createError({ statusCode: 404 })` (Nuxt renders the error page), or wrap the fetch+title in one small `useResourcePage` composable.
Move the em-dash formatting into the server payload (as done for the effect fallback at pokeapi.ts:449) or into a shared util.

findings.issue: The dex-number padding rule is implemented in the component (`#` + padStart(4,'0')) while the server already formats `dexNumber` the same way at pokeapi.ts:408.
findings.suggestion: Include `dexNumber` in `SpeciesSummary` so the formatting rule lives only in pokeapi.ts.

findings.issue: `VALID_TYPE_NAMES` hardcodes the 18 type names in source; the API already returns them, and a data change (new type) requires a code edit.
findings.suggestion: Filter `/type/` results by excluding `stellar`, `unknown` and `shadow` rather than allow-listing names.

findings.issue: All component styling (577 lines) lives in one global stylesheet rather than Nuxt scoped styles, so removing a feature strands dead CSS and styles are not colocated with their components.
findings.suggestion: Move per-component rules into scoped `<style>` blocks (or per-component CSS files) and keep only tokens and layout in the global sheet.

summary: This is idiomatic, current-stable Nuxt 4 (4.6.3) with an excellent server/client seam: one util file owns all upstream knowledge and every card derives from a single central summary, so data-source changes and sprite-style data bugs are one-file fixes. The costs are duplicated boilerplate — card-list markup on four pages, near-identical page-data functions, a five-times-repeated type-label Map and a dead helper — and an untyped `any` payload contract that loses the compile-time checks Nuxt 4.6 can give. Extending with another Moves-shaped section therefore means copy-paste rather than reuse, but nothing is entangled or hard to find.
